subject: Media Literacy
title: Repetition and the Big Lie
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Repetition and the Big Lie.

hook.text: Say 'the election was stolen' ten thousand times and millions will believe it without evidence.

buildup.text: Repetition is the simplest and most effective propaganda technique. It requires no proof, just persistence.

discovery.text: The 'illusory truth effect' has been confirmed in dozens of studies — repetition creates belief.

twist.text: Correcting a false claim actually strengthens it — because correction requires repeating the original claim.

climax.text: In the age of social media, a lie can circle the globe a million times before the truth gets started.

punchline.text: A lie repeated often enough isn't truth. But it feels like it.

quiz.question: Why can correcting false claims actually backfire?
options: Correction requires repeating the original claim, reinforcing it
